196.subject: Botany
196.text: What happens to a cell during M phase of cell cycle?
196.sol: During G₁ phase, the cell is in resting state and the nucleocytoplasmic index is stable. During the S phase of the cell cycle, DNA replicates, consequently nucleocytoplasmic index increases due to increase in nuclear volume. During G₂ phase, the cell is again stable. During M phase, nucleocytoplasmic index decreases. After M phase or mitosis when the cell divides, nucleoplasmic index returns to normal.

71511.subject: Biology
71511.text: In angiosperms, when the pollen tube enters the ovule through micropyle, it is called ______.
71511.sol: In angiosperms, the entry of the pollen tube into the ovule can occur through different routes. When the pollen tube enters the ovule through the micropyle, the process is known as porogamy. This is the most common type of pollen tube entry. Chalazogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube through the chalazal end. Mesogamy refers to the entry of the pollen tube through the integuments or funiculus. Siphonogamy is the general term for fertilization involving a pollen tube. Answer: porogamy

71561.subject: Biology
71561.text: If any solute is added in pure water, what will be the effect on the value of water potential?
options: Value of water potential is increased.
Value of water potential is decreased.
There is no change in its value.
Value of water potential becomes more than D.P.D.
71561.sol: Pure water has the maximum water potential, which is zero at standard temperature and pressure. When a solute is added to pure water, the concentration of free water molecules decreases, which lowers the free energy of water. This results in a decrease in the water potential, making it negative. Therefore, the value of water potential is decreased. Answer: Value of water potential is decreased.

72458.text: When light waves travel from rarer medium to denser medium, the qunatities which get changed are
72458.sol: When light travels from one medium to another, the frequency of the light remains constant as it is a characteristic property of the source of light. The velocity of light changes depending on the refractive index of the medium, given by v = c . Since v = and the frequency is constant, the wavelength must also change proportionally with the velocity. Thus, velocity and wavelength change when light travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium. Answer: velocity and wavelength.

84246.text: Low Ca ²⁺ in the body fluid may be the cause of
84246.sol: The usual cause of tetany is lack of calcium. But excess of phosphate can also trigger the spasms. Hypoparathyroidism (hyposecretion of parathormone) can lead to tetany. In this, some skeletal muscles, usually of hands and feet fail to relax after a contraction and remain in sustained condition. Tetany of laryngeal, thoracic and phrenic muscles which help in breathing causes death, because the patient fails to breath (asphyxia).

It acts as a depressant and slows down action of the nervous system.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
122360.sol: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic animals, e.g., coelenterates.

123135.subject: Botany
123135.text: Which of the following is correctly matched?
123135.sol: Fasciculated root is a type of adventitious root. In this case, roots are swollen which occur in clusters from lower nodes of stems, e.g., Asparagus, Dahlia, etc.

123591.subject: Botany
123591.text: What is the characteristic event of prophase?
options: Chromosomal material condenses to form compact mitotic chromosomes
Centrosome begins to move towards the same pole of the cell
123591.sol: The completion of prophase can thus be marked by the following characteristic events: Chromosomal material condenses to form compact mitotic chromosomes. Chromosomes are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the centromere. Centrosome which had undergone duplication during interphase, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell. Each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters. The two asters together with spindle fibres forms mitotic apparatus.

123593.subject: Botany
123593.text: What happens to the centrosome during prophase?
options: It remains at the same location
It begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell
It begins to move towards the same pole of the cell
123593.sol: Prophase which is the first stage of karyokinesis of mitosis follows the S and G2 phases of interphase. In the S and G2 phases the new DNA molecules formed are not distinct but intertwined. Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material. The chromosomal material becomes untangled during the process of chromatin condensation. The centrosome, which had undergone duplication during S phase of interphase, now begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell.

123650.subject: Botany
123650.text: What is the purpose of meiosis?
123650.sol: The production of offspring by sexual reproduction includes the fusion of two gametes, each with a complete haploid set of chromosomes. Gametes are formed from specialised diploid cells. This specialised kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half results in the production of haploid daughter cells. This kind of division is called meiosis. Meiosis ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms whereas fertilisation restores the diploid phase. We come

123815.subject: Botany
123815.text: During the pachytene stage of prophase I, recombination nodules appear on the bivalents to mark the sites of crossing over. Which of the following correctly describes the nature of this crossing over process?
options: It is a non-enzymatic physical breakage and reunion of chromatids.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving the enzyme recombinase.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving DNA ligase only.
It is an enzyme-mediated process primarily involving RNA polymerase.
123815.sol: According to NCERT, crossing over occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis. It is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, which mark the sites where the exchange of genetic material takes place between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is strictly an enzyme-mediated process. The specific enzyme complex involved in this recombination process is called recombinase. It does not occur through mere physical breakage without enzymes, nor are DNA ligase or R

123896.subject: Botany
123896.text: A diploid meiocyte in the G₁ phase of its cell cycle has 16 chromosomes and its DNA content is 20 pg. Which of the following correctly describes the configuration of this cell during the Pachytene stage of meiosis I?
options: 8 bivalents, 32 chromatids, 20 pg of DNA, and the appearance of recombination nodules
16 bivalents, 32 chromatids, 40 pg of DNA, and the formation of the synaptonemal complex
8 bivalents, 16 chromatids, 40 pg of DNA, and the formation of the synaptonemal complex
8 bivalents, 32 chromatids, 40 pg of DNA, and the appearance of recombination nodules
123896.sol: In the G₁ phase, the meiocyte has 2n = 16 chromosomes and a DNA content of 20 pg. During the S phase, DNA replication occurs, doubling the DNA content to 40 pg, but the chromosome number remains the same (16 chromosomes). Each chromosome now consists of two sister chromatids. During the Pachytene stage of Prophase I, the homologous chromosomes are paired. Since there are 16 chromosomes, they form 8 pairs, which are called bivalents (or tetrads). The total number of chromatids is 16 2 = 32 chromatids. The DNA conten

124332.subject: Botany
124332.text: A newly synthesized secretory glycoprotein is being processed by a eukaryotic cell. Which of the following represents the correct chronological pathway of the structures it passes through from its inception to its release?
options: Rough endoplasmic reticulum cis face of Golgi trans face of Golgi Secretory vesicle
Rough endoplasmic reticulum trans face of Golgi cis face of Golgi Secretory vesicle
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum cis face of Golgi trans face of Golgi Secretory vesicle
Cytoplasm cis face of Golgi trans face of Golgi Rough endoplasmic reticulum
124332.sol: The protein backbone of a secretory glycoprotein is synthesized by ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). These proteins are then packaged into vesicles that fuse with the convex cis (forming) face of the Golgi apparatus. Inside the Golgi cisternae, the proteins are modified (glycosylated) into glycoproteins as they move towards the concave trans (maturing) face. Finally, they are packaged into secretory vesicles at the trans face and released for exocytosis. Reversing the cis and trans faces

124571.subject: Botany
124571.text: How many gibberellins have been reported from various organisms?
124571.sol: Gibberellins are another kind of promotery PGR. There are more than 100 gibberellins reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants. They are denoted as GA1 , GA2 , GA3 and so on.All GAs are acidic. They produce a wide range of physiological responses in the plants. Their ability to cause an increase in length of axis is used to increase the length of grapes stalks.

124778.subject: Botany
124778.text: Who among the following scientists was the first to successfully isolate auxin, and from which specific plant source was it obtained?
options: Charles Darwin from the coleoptiles of canary grass
F.W. Went from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings
E. Kurosawa from infected rice seedlings
F. Skoog from the internodal segments of tobacco stems
124778.sol: According to NCERT, while Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin first observed the phenomenon of phototropism in the coleoptiles of canary grass, it was F.W. Went who successfully isolated the active substance (auxin) from the tips of coleoptiles of oat (Avena) seedlings. The other options represent different milestones: Charles Darwin is associated with the initial observation of phototropism, E. Kurosawa with the discovery of gibberellins in rice seedlings, and F. Skoog with the discovery of cytokinins using tobacco

124812.subject: Botany
124812.text: Assertion : Vernalization is acceleration of subsquent flowering by low temperature treatment. Reason : Site of vernalization is apical meristem.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
124812.sol: Term vernalization was first given by T.D. Lysenko (1928). In colder countries, there are cereals of 2 physiological types, i.e., winter cereals and spring cereals. Winter cereals are sown in winter and flower in following summer whereas spring cereals are sown in spring and flower in summer. If winter cereal is sown in spring, it shows vegetative growth but does not flower unless it receives low temperature of winter. But winter cereal can be converted into spring cereal by providing artificial low temperature tre

124863.text: A plasmolysed cell can be deplasmolysed by placing it in

Glucose has been broken down to release CO2 and eight molecules of NADH + H+; two of FADH2 have been synthesised besides just two molecules of ATP in TCA cycle. 2. The metabolic pathway through which the electron passes from one carrier to another is called electron transport system and it is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. 3. The metabolic

The metabolic pathway through which the electron passes from one carrier to another is called electron transport system and it is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Cytochrome c is a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane and acts as a mobile carrier for transfer of electrons between complex III and IV. Complex IV refers

125290.subject: Botany
125290.text: Stomatal opening in plants occurs due to influx of
125290.sol: It has been now experimentally proved that opening of stomata is an energy consuming process and not closing. The turgidity of guard cells is usually controalled by K ⁺, Cl ⁻ and H ⁺ . The opening of stomata is initiated by excretion of H ⁺ by guard cells, intake of K ⁺ and Cl ⁻ and closing is controlled by abscisic acid.

125378.subject: Botany
options: Synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of darkness
Synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light
Breakdown of ATP to ADP and inorganic phosphate
Conversion of light energy into thermal energy
125378.sol: : Living organisms have the capability of extracting energy from oxidisable substances and store this in the form of bond energy. Special substances like ATP, carry this energy in their chemical bonds. The process through which ATP is synthesised by cells (in mitochondria and chloroplasts) is named phosphorylation. Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light. When the two photosystems work in a series, first PS II and then the PS I, a process called non-cyc

125472.subject: Botany
125472.text: According to Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors, what determines the rate of a chemical process affected by more than one factor?
options: The factor that is at its maximum value
The factor nearest to its minimal value
The factor that changes the most
The factor that is most constant
125472.sol: When several factors affect any [bio] chemical process, Blackman’s (1905) Law of Limiting Factors comes into effect. This states the following: If a chemical process is affected by more than one factor, then its rate will be determined by the factor which is nearest to its minimal value: it is the factor which directly affects the process if its quantity is changed. For example, despite the presence of a green leaf and optimal light and CO2 conditions, the plant may not photosynthesise if the temperature is very lo

125579.subject: Botany
125579.text: Component Function A. Photosystem I (PS I) 1. Absorption peak at 680 nm, known as P680. B. Photosystem II (PS II) 2. Absorption peak at 700 nm, known as P700. C. Light Harvesting Complex (LHC. 3. Organizes pigments into complexes to absorb different wavelengths of light. D. Reaction Centre 4. Site where high-energy chemical intermediates are formed.
125579.sol: A - 2: Photosystem I (PS I) has a reaction centre chlorophyll a with an absorption peak at 700 nm, known as P700. B - 1: Photosystem II (PS II) has a reaction centre chlorophyll a with an absorption peak at 680 nm, known as P680. C - 3: The Light Harvesting Complex (LHC) organizes pigments to absorb various wavelengths of light. D - 4: The reaction centre is where high-energy chemical intermediates, ATP and NADPH, are formed.

125585.subject: Botany
125585.text: Pathway Components Functions A. RuBP 1. The molecule that accepts CO2 to begin the Calvin cycle. B. 3-PGA 2. A stable organic intermediate produced from the carboxylation of RuBP. C. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P) 3.Energy carriers used in the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle. D. ATP and NADPH 4. The product formed after the reduction of 3-PGA.
125585.sol: A - 1: RuBP is the molecule that accepts CO2 at the start of the Calvin cycle. B - 2: 3-PGA is the stable organic intermediate produced from the carboxylation of RuBP. C - 4: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P) is the product formed after the reduction of 3-PGA. D - 3: ATP and NADPH are energy carriers used in the reduction phase of the Calvin cycle.

125683.subject: Botany
125683.text: The saturation point of CO ₂ in C ₄ plants is
125683.sol: The optimum CO ₂ concentration for C ₄ plants is 360 l / L or 360 ppm .

126163.subject: Botany
126163.text: Parts of Dicot embryo Location/Features A. Radicle 1. Epicotyl terminates into it B. Hypocotyl 2. Portion of axis above the cotyledons C. Plumule 3. Hypocotyl terminates into it D. Epicotyl 4. Portion of axis below the cotyledons
126163.sol: Typical dicotyledonous embryo (Figure 1.14a), consists of an embryonal axis and two cotyledons. The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or stem tip. The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is hypocotyl that terminates at its lower end in the radicle or root tip. The root tip is covered with a root cap.

126220.subject: Botany
126220.text: Water hyacinth and water lily are common aquatic plants. Which of the following statements correctly describes the pollination mechanism and floral features in these plants?
options: The pollen grains are protected by a mucilaginous covering and are carried passively by water currents.
The female flowers remain submerged in water and receive long, ribbon-like pollen grains.
The female flowers reach the surface of the water by long stalks and receive pollen carried by water currents.
The flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind.
126220.sol: Although water hyacinth and water lily are aquatic plants, they do not use water as a pollinating agent. According to NCERT, in a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind, similar to most land plants. Female flowers reaching the surface to receive pollen via water currents is seen in Vallisneria. Submerged female flowers receiving ribbon-like pollen is characteristic of seagrasses like Zostera. Pollen protecte

126321.subject: Botany
126321.text: The pollen grains of rice and wheat lose their viability in minutes of their release
126321.sol: Pollen viability is the period for which pollen grains retain the ability to germinate. Pollen viability is little in flowers which are pollinated in bud condition. It is 30 minutes in rice and wheat. It depends upon environmental conditions of temperature and humidity.

126895.subject: Botany
126895.text: From the following groups, select the one which has only secondary metabolites?
126895.sol: Secondary metabolites are derivatives of primary metabolites which have no direct function in growth and development of plants. These compounds are accessory rather than central to the functioning, e.g., arbrin, cellulose, gums, diterpenes, carotenoids, curcumin, rubber etc. Arginine, tyrosine, glycine, serine and phenylalanine are amino acids, which are primary metabolites.

127978.subject: Zoology
127978.text: Where is the organ of smell located in frogs?
127978.sol: Frog has different types of sense organs, namely organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), smell (nasal epithelium), vision (eyes) and hearing (tympanum with internal ears). Out of these, eyes and internal ears are well-organised structures and the rest are cellular aggregations around nerve endings. Eyes in a frog are a pair of spherical structures situated in the orbit in skull. These are simple eyes (possessing only one unit). External ear is absent in frogs and only tympanum can be seen externally

128085.subject: Zoology
128085.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Cockroach is a uricotelic animal. Reason (R): In cockroach, Malpighian tubules absorb nitrogenous wastes from haemolymph and convert them into uric acid, which is excreted out through the hindgut. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct.
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
128085.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because cockroaches excrete uric acid as their primary nitrogenous waste, making them uricotelic. Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact physiological mechanism for the assertion. The Malpighian tubules, which are the primary excretory organs in cockroaches, absorb nitrogenous waste products from the haemolymph and convert them into uric acid. This uric acid is then eliminated through the hindgut. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and Reason is the correct explana

128152.subject: Zoology
128152.text: In the circulatory system of a frog, the single ventricle opens into a sac-like structure to pump blood out of the heart. Identify this structure and its anatomical position on the heart.
options: Sinus venosus located on the dorsal side
Conus arteriosus located on the ventral side
Conus arteriosus located on the dorsal side
Sinus venosus located on the ventral side
128152.sol: In a frog's heart, the ventricle pumps blood out by opening into a sac-like structure called the conus arteriosus, which is located on the ventral side of the heart. The sinus venosus is a triangular structure that joins the right atrium to receive deoxygenated blood, not the structure the ventricle opens into. Answer: Conus arteriosus located on the ventral side

128266.subject: Zoology
128266.sol: Endocrine glands lack ducts and are hence, called ductless glands. Their secretions are called hormones. The classical definition of hormone as a chemical produced by endocrine glands and released into the blood and transported to a distantly located target organ has current scientific definition as follows: Hormones are non-nutrient chemicals which act as intercellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. The new definition covers a number of new molecules in addition to the hormones secreted by the organ

128404.sol: A, B, C and D, E and F respectively are Pineal, Thyroid and Parathyroid, Thymus, Pancreas, Adrenal, Testis

128548.subject: Zoology
128548.text: Disease/Condition Cause A. Diabetes Insipidus 1. Overproduction of GH in adults B. Dwarfism 2. Overproduction of GH in children C. Acromegaly 3. Underproduction of ADH D. Gigantism 4. Underproduction of GH
128548.sol: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications, and premature death if unchecked. An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water

128717.subject: Zoology
128717.text: Assertion : Escherichia coli, Shigella sp. and Salmonella sp. are all responsible for diarrhoeal disease. Reason : Dehydration is common to all types of diarrhoeal diseases and adequate supply of fluids electrolytes should be ensured.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
128717.sol: E.coli, Shigella sp. and Salmonella species are all bacteria which are responsible for the diarrhoea diseases. Diarrhoea is a frequent bowel evacuation or the passage of abnormally soft or liquid faeces. It may be caused by intestinal infections, other form of intestinal inflammation (such as Colitis or Crohn's disease), malabsorption, anxiety and the irritable bowel syndrome. Severe or prolonged diarrhoea may lead to excess losses of fluid, salts and nutrients in the faeces. Dehydration (whose symptoms includes gr

128746.subject: Zoology
128746.text: Epithelial cells of the intestine involved in food absorption have on their surface
128746.sol: The mucosa and sub-mucosa of small intestine are thrown into folds. Surfaces of these folds is covered by fine, fingerlike projections of the epithelium. These projections are called villi. In addition, the epithelial cells of the villi are covered on their exposed surface by cytoplasmic projections called microvilli.

128814.subject: Zoology
128814.sol: group ‘O’ blood can be donated to persons with any other blood group and hence ‘O’ group individuals are called ‘universal donors’. Persons with ‘AB’ group can accept blood from persons with AB as well as the other groups of blood. Therefore, such persons are called ‘universal recipients’.

128841.subject: Zoology
128841.text: What type of circulatory system is present in annelids and chordates?
128841.sol: The circulatory patterns are of two types – open or closed. Open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system in which the blood pumped by the heart is always circulated through a closed network of blood vessels . This pattern is considered to be more advantageous as the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated.

129172.subject: Zoology
129172.text: What happens to the activities of nerves, lungs, heart and kidney when physical exercise is stopped?
options: They gradually return to their normal conditions.
129172.sol: Coordination refers to the process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions in order to maintain homeostasis When physical exercise is stopped, the activities of nerves, lungs, heart and kidney gradually return to their normal conditions. The neural system and the endocrine system jointly coordinate and integrate all the activities of the organs so that they function in a synchronised fashionThe neural system provides an organized network of point-to-point connections for quick coo

129409.subject: Zoology
129409.text: A frog has its brain crushed. But when pinched on the leg, The leg draws away. It is an example of
129409.sol: A simple reflex action is a nerve mediated spontaneous automatic and involuntary response to a stimulus acting on a specific receptor without consulting the will of the animal. Conditioned reflexes are those reflex actions that are not present at birth but develop later in life through learning, habit, experience or regular association of an indifferent stimulus with unconditioned stimulus.

129617.subject: Zoology

129617.sol: DCT is also capable of reabsorption of HCO3– and selective secretion of hydrogen and potassium ions and NH3 to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood.

Statement (b) is correct as Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor that increases glomerular blood pressure and GFR. Statement (c) is incorrect because Aldosterone causes the reabsorption of Na ⁺ and water from the distal parts of the tubule, not the proximal convoluted tubule. Statement (d) is correct because ANF causes vasodilation and decreases blood p

129891.subject: Zoology
129891.text: Where is the highest concentration of carbonic anhydrase found?
129891.sol: CO2 is carried by haemoglobin as carbamino-haemoglobin (about 20-25 per cent). This binding is related to the partial pressure of CO2. pO2 is a major factor which could affect this binding. When pCO2 is high and pO2 is low as in the tissues, more binding of carbon dioxide occurs whereas, when the pCO2 is low and pO2 is high as in the alveoli, dissociation of CO2 from carbamino-haemoglobin takes place, i.e., CO2 which is bound to haemoglobin from the tissues is delivered at the alveoli . 129922.subject: Zoology
129922.text: What is the main mechanism for the exchange of O₂ and CO₂ in the body?
129922.sol: Exchange of O₂ and CO₂ at the alveoli and tissues occur by diffusion. Rate of diffusion is dependent on the partial pressure gradients of O₂ (pO₂) and CO₂ (pCO₂), their solubility as well as the thickness of the diffusion surface. Alveoli are the primary sites of exchange of gases . Exchange of gases also occur between blood and tissues. O2 and CO2 are exchanged in these sites by simple diffusion mainly based on pressure/concentration gradient. Solubility of the gases as well as the thickness of the membranes invol

130251.subject: Zoology
130251.text: What is the structure to which each rib is attached ventrally?
130251.sol: .The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The skull is composed of two sets of bones, cranial and facial, that total to 22 bones.Each vertebra has a central hollow portion (neural canal) through which the spinal cord passes. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions.There are 12 pairs of ribs in the human body. Each rib

130311.subject: Zoology
130311.text: Choose the correct statement taking help from the given diagram: Assertion: Mechanism of muscle contraction is explained by sliding-filaments theory. Reason: Contraction of muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of thick filaments over the thin filaments.

If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is wrong but Reason is true.
130311.sol: Mechanism of muscle contraction is best explained by the sliding filament theory which states that contraction of a muscle fibre takes place by the sliding of the thin filaments over the thick filaments.

130764.subject: Zoology
130764.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding contraceptive methods. List-I List-II (A) Lippes loop (I) Hormone-releasing IUD (B) Multiload 375 (II) Copper-releasing IUD (C) LNG-20 (III) Non-medicated IUD (D) Vaults (IV) Barrier method Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Multiload 375 is a copper-releasing IUD that suppresses sperm motility and fertilising capacity. LNG-20 is a hormone-releasing IUD that makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. Vaults are barrier methods made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV). Answer:

130766.subject: Zoology
130766.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) is not a suitable treatment for females with bilaterally blocked fallopian tubes, even if the male partner has a very low sperm count. Reason (R): IUI involves artificially introducing semen into the uterus, which requires at least one patent (open) fallopian tube f
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
130766.sol: Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) is an in-vivo fertilization technique where semen is artificially introduced into the uterus to assist couples where the male partner has a low sperm count. For fertilization to occur naturally, the sperm must swim up from the uterus into the ampullary region of the fallopian tube to meet the ovum. If the fallopian tubes are bilaterally blocked, the sperm cannot reach the ovum, making IUI ineffective. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains t

130848.subject: Zoology
130848.text: What are the hormones produced by the ovaries?
130848.sol: The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries along with a pair of oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and the external genitalia located in pelvic region. These parts of the system along with a pair of the mammary glands are integrated structurally and functionally to support the processes of ovulation, fertilisation, pregnancy, birth and child care. Ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones (ovarian hormones). The ovaries are located o

131298.subject: Zoology
131298.text: Which of the following pairs of structures in the human female reproductive system is explicitly characterized by the presence of a cushion of fatty tissue or a variable amount of fat?
131298.sol: According to NCERT, the mons pubis is a cushion of fatty tissue covered by skin and pubic hair. Similarly, the mammary glands are paired structures that contain glandular tissue and a variable amount of fat. The labia majora are described as fleshy folds of tissue, not fatty tissue. The labia minora are paired folds of tissue. The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure. Internal organs like the uterus and ovaries are not primarily characterized by fat deposits in this context. Therefore, the correct pair is the m

131461.text: What was the result of Hershey and Chase's experiments regarding the transfer of genetic material from the virus to the bacteria?
options: Proteins entered the bacteria from the viruses
RNA entered the bacteria from the viruses
DNA entered the bacteria from the viruses
Neither proteins nor DNA entered the bacteria from the viruses

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
133621.sol: A small, glandular, blind pouch of lymphatic tissue, the bursa lies on the dorsal side of the cloaca. It is lined with endoderm, and opens into the proctodaeum. In a young bird, bursa fabricii forms lymphocytes, and probably it produces antibodies and protects against local infection, but it atrophies in the adult before sexual maturity. It is also called cloacal thymus, because like thymus, it secretes lymphocytes. Thus it is not related with flight adaptation, rather it helps in immunity.

95652.subject: Botany
95652.text: The smallest disease-causing agent is ________, and it is made up of ___________
95652.sol: Prions are discovered by Prusiner in 1982. They are the smallest infectious protein particles which lack nucleic acid. Prions are modified hydrophobic glycoproteins that are resistant to protease action compared with normal proteins; they function as infectious agents. Prions change normal proteins to an infectious form, and they are found to cause diseases in animals and not in plants.

95756.subject: Botany
options: causes an algal bloom where its rapid multiplication changes the sea colour
leads to the formation of diatomaceous earth
behaves like a heterotroph in the absence of sunlight
has an infectious spore-like stage in their life cycle and has a staggering effect on the human population.
95756.sol: Red tide is caused due to dinoflagellate Gonyaulax. During favourable season Gonyaulax multiplies rapidly forming huge mass which gives red colour to water known as red tide. It secretes toxic substance called saxitoxin in water which results death of large number of marine fishes.

96172.subject: Botany
96172.text: Find out the number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA in a spore mother cell of Bryophytes in G 2 stage (If the spore contains 5 chromosomes and 5pg of DNA) -
96172.sol: Spore mother cell is diploid and spore is haploid. If spore has 5 chromosomes and 5pg DNA than the spore mother cell has 10 chromosomes and 10pg DNA in the G 1 phase. Since DNA replication occurs during S phase but chromosome number remains unchanged. Thus chromosome in the G 2 phase is 10 and the quantity of DNA is 20 pg.

96573.subject: Botany
96573.text: Identify the correct sequence of succession in a hydrosere.
options: Free-floating hydrophytes, sedges, phytoplankton, rooted hydrophytes, grasses and trees.
Phytoplankton, rooted submerged hydrophytes, floating hydrophytes, reed swamp, marsh meadow and trees.
Phytoplankton, sedges, free-floating hydrophytes, rooted hydrophytes, grasses and trees.
Phytoplankton, free-floating hydrophytes, rooted hydrophytes; sedges, grasses and trees.
96573.sol: In the primary succession in water the pioneers are small phytoplanktons, they are replaced with time by rooted submerged plants then by floating hydrophytes, sedges grasses and finally trees. Phytoplanktons are pioneer community and trees are the climax community which at the end becomes stable.

96624.subject: Botany
96624.text: The rate at which light energy is converted to the chemical energy of organic molecules is:
96624.sol: The rate at which organic molecules are formed in a green plant is called gross productivity. Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration.

96872.subject: Botany
96872.text: Which of the following is not a medicinal plant?
96872.sol: Muliathi ( Glycirrhizae ), a member of Fabaceae, Aloe vera, a member of Liliaceae family, and Belladonna ( Atropa belladonna ), a member of Solanaceae family, are all medicinal plants. Indigofera commonly called the Nile is used to obtain dye.

96963.subject: Botany
96963.text: In which of the following, replum can be seen?
96963.sol: Replum is a false septum like structure present in the fruit that separates the two valves of the fruit. It is observed commonly in the group Brassica. Mustard is a classic example to show replum.

97442.subject: Botany
97442.text: Which of the following is dioecious?
97442.sol: "Dioecious" and "monoecious" are terms that refer to the reproductive structure developed in a single organism. They are adjectives used in horticultural descriptions. Dioecious describes a plant group that includes distinct male and female plants. Monoecious describes a single plant that bears both male and female reproductive structures.

97516.subject: Botany
97516.text: Which of the following structure is not related to the life cycle of Funaria?
97516.sol: Funaria is a Bryophyte in which the spore germinates to form a filamentous branched creeping structure called protonema, which is the primary stage, from which develops a secondary stage on which sex organs antheridium and archegonium are formed. Prothallus is a gametophyte found in Pteridophytes.

97527.subject: Botany
97527.text: Which of the following algae is used to prepare culture medium to grow microbe?
97527.sol: Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water-holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageen (red algae) which are used commercially. Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies. Chlorella a unicellular alga rich in proteins is used as food supplement even by space travellers.

97836.subject: Botany
97836.text: Select the correct statement from the following given statements. (I) Properties of tissues are present in the constituent cell and arise as a result of interactions among them. (II) Properties of cellular organelles are present in the molecular constituents of the organelles and arise as a result of interactions among them. (III) Living organisms are system capable of responding to external stimuli.
options: I, II and III are correct
97836.sol: Cellular organelles characteristics are not present in the molecular components of the organelle but form as a result of interactions among the molecular components making the organelle. Living organisms are self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli. Properties of tissues are not presenting the constituent cells but arise as a result of interactions among the constituent cells.

98186.subject: Chemistry
98186.text: Which of the following carbohydrate is a reducing sugar?
98186.sol: A sugar is classified as a reducing sugar only if it has an open-chain form with an aldehyde group or a free hemiacetal group. Monosaccharides which contain an aldehyde group are known as aldoses, and those with a ketone group are known as ketoses. All monosaccharides are called reducing sugars.

309662.text: Arrange the following alkyl bromides in decreasing order of their reactivity towards nucleophilic substitution with alcoholic AgCN : (I) CH ₃- CH ₂- Br (II) (III)
309662.sol: The reaction of alkyl halides with alcoholic AgCN predominantly follows the S_N1 mechanism. This is because the Ag ^+ ion acts as a Lewis acid, coordinating with the leaving halogen atom and facilitating the cleavage of the C-Br bond to form a carbocation intermediate (along with the precipitation of AgBr ). The reactivity of an alkyl halide in an S_N1 reaction is directly proportional to the stability of the carbocation formed. The carbocations generated from the given alkyl bromides are: (I) CH₃-CH₂-Br CH₃-CH₂^+

N1 is protonated because imidazole is an aromatic heterocycle where n=1 as per Hückel's rule.
N3 is protonated because its lone pair resides in an sp ² hybridized orbital and is not involved in aromaticit

309500.sol: In imidazole, there are two nitrogen atoms: N1 and N3. The nitrogen atom N1 (pyrrole-like) is bonded to a hydrogen atom. Its lone pair of electrons resides in an unhybridized p-orbital and is delocalized into the ring to complete the aromatic sextet ( 6 electrons), satisfying Hückel's rule ( 4n+2 ). Because this lone pair is involved in aromaticity, it is not readily available for protonation. Protonating N1 would disrupt the aromatic stability of the molecule. 6a7a1ff8f993090e87705125.text: In two separate experiments, photons of energy 116 eV and 20 eV are incident on hydrogen atoms in their ground state.
